chief_complaint: delusions of FBI microchip tracking thoughts
hpi_details: A 56-year-old female presents to the clinic with delusions of fbi microchip tracking thoughts. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She believes government surveillance agents secretly implanted an electronic microchip in her body to monitor her thoughts.
concerns: She is worried that the people tracking her thoughts will leak her private information or manipulate her actions.
expectations: She hopes the doctor will order an X-ray or body scan to pinpoint the implant and refer her to have it surgically removed.

core_concepts: New-onset psychosis requires urgent safety assessment and evaluation for delirium, substance or medication effects, neurologic disease, mood disorders, and primary psychotic disorders before assigning a diagnosis.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Management emphasizes urgent safety assessment, medical and substance evaluation, and psychiatric consultation; antipsychotic treatment is individualized after evaluation.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: delusions of FBI microchip tracking thoughts

Key HPI features: A 56-year-old female presents to the clinic with delusions of fbi microchip tracking thoughts. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical and neurologic examination, vital signs, and targeted evaluation for secondary causes of psychosis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out First-Episode Psychosis / Schizophrenia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bipolar I with psychotic features without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Command auditory hallucinations.
management_principles: Urgent safety assessment, evaluation for secondary causes, and psychiatric consultation; consider antipsychotic treatment after evaluation
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of delusions of FBI microchip tracking thoughts. HPI: schizophrenia.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical and neurologic examination, vital signs, medication and substance review, and targeted testing for secondary causes of psychosis.
reference_soap.assessment: First-episode psychosis; schizophrenia-spectrum illness remains a differential diagnosis pending exclusion of secondary causes.
reference_soap.plan: Perform urgent safety assessment and evaluate for delirium, substance or medication effects, and medical or neurologic causes. Obtain psychiatric consultation and consider antipsychotic treatment after this evaluation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of first-episode psychosis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for first-episode psychosis and secondary causes
Implement evidence-based management plan: safety assessment, secondary-cause evaluation, and psychiatric consultation

teaching.diagnosis: First-episode psychosis — assess for secondary causes
teaching.one_liner: New psychosis at age 56 requires urgent safety assessment and evaluation for delirium, medication/substance effects, neurologic disease, and mood or primary psychotic disorders before assigning schizophrenia.
red_flags: Command hallucinations or risk to self/others
New focal neurologic signs or severe headache

must_ask.say: Have you had thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else, or heard voices telling you to act?
Have you had confusion, memory changes, fever, or symptoms that come and go during the day?
Have you started any medicines or used alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other substances recently?

history.answer: Doctor, I came because someone has implanted an FBI microchip in my head and they are tracking all my thoughts.
It started about three weeks ago, and it has been gradually getting worse every day.
I have been feeling constantly exhausted and run down since this all started.
I can feel the chip monitoring my brain, sending signals to government agents who watch what I am thinking.
No, I haven't heard any voices talking or whispering, and I don't see things that aren't there.
No, there are no voices telling me to do anything.
I feel like my private thoughts are being broadcasted outward, but strangers on television aren't talking directly about me.
I have been staying home more and have trouble keeping up with housework, but I still dress and wash myself.
No, my mood has not been unusually high or irritable, and my thoughts aren't racing.
No, I haven't gone on any shopping sprees, taken financial gambles, or done anything reckless.
I feel drained and stressed by the surveillance, but I haven't had deep bouts of depression or lost interest in life before this.
The belief that the microchip is tracking me stays constant whether I feel okay or upset.
No, I would never harm myself, and I have never thought about ending my life.
No, I have no intention to hurt anyone else, and I don't keep any weapons.
No, my thinking has been clear, and I don't get confused about where I am or what day it is.
No, I haven't had any severe headaches, seizures, or fainting spells.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, heart palpitations, or unexplained weight loss.
I wake up several times during the night worrying about being watched, but there was no major stressful event right before this began.
I know for a fact that federal agents planted a microchip inside me while I was asleep to track everything I think.
I'm terrified that whoever is listening in will broadcast my private thoughts online or force me to do something terrible.
I want you to do an X-ray or full-body scan so we can prove where the chip is and get a surgeon to cut it out.
No, I have never used illicit drugs, stimulants, marijuana, or anything like that.
I have never been prescribed any mood stabilizers, antipsychotics, or antidepressants.
I have always been healthy and have never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid trouble.
I have never had any surgeries and have never stayed overnight in a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only have an occasional glass of wine when dining out, maybe once or twice a month, and haven't had any recently.
I work as an administrative assistant at an accounting firm and live with my husband.
My periods stopped completely five years ago when I turned fifty-one, and I have had no bleeding since.
No one in my family has ever suffered from schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, severe depression, or committed suicide.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg, pulse 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, and temperature 36.7°C.
Alert and neatly dressed female, appears tired and guarded, with intermittent eye contact but no psychomotor agitation.

Fully oriented to person, place, and time; speech is fluent and normal in rate, without loosening of associations or tangentiality; endorses persecutory belief regarding microchip thought monitoring without active perceptual disturbances.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light; extraocular movements intact without nystagmus or facial asymmetry.
Normal bulk and 5/5 strength throughout all four extremities without focal weakness or spasticity.
Intact sensation to light touch and pinprick symmetrically across all dermatomes.
Normal finger-to-nose testing, steady tandem gait, and negative Romberg sign.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and smooth with no palpable nodules or bruits.
Neck is supple with no rigidity; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
